title: Each strongly connected component rescans every graph edge
reasoning: The mass calculation iterates all internal graph edges for every strongly connected component. An acyclic graph has one component per node, making this phase O(VE), or quadratic for a sparse chain, despite component detection itself being linear. Large ordinary call graphs therefore incur unnecessary scoring cost.
reproduction: Score production call graphs formed as chains of increasing length. Every singleton component scans the full edge set even though its internal mass is zero.
recommendation: Assign component membership first, then accumulate component masses in a single edge pass when both endpoints belong to the same component.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were included; correctness checks on small graphs would return the expected masses despite the repeated scans.
suggestedRegressionTest: Cover chains, disconnected nodes, cycles, and self-loops, verifying identical masses and that edge processing grows linearly rather than once per component.
